audit.title: Automation Architecture

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: The opening leads with a diagram reference ("The following diagram describes…") rather than a self-contained definition of what Chainlink Automation *is*. "How it works" opens well: "Automation Nodes form a peer-to-peer network using Chainlink's OCR3 protocol." A one-sentence canonical definition at the very top would help.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Clean H1→H2, 0 level skips, 4 coherent sections (measured). No tables or bullets, which is acceptable at this length but a summary table of actors (Registry, Automation Nodes, Upkeeps) would aid extraction.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Weak. 0 numerals, 0 units, 0 versions (measured); vague quantifiers "some" and "significant" flagged. No node counts, consensus thresholds, redundancy figures, or supported-network counts.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: 3 internal links, 0 external/primary (measured). "OCR3 protocol" and "transaction manager" are named but never linked to their canonical spec/definition pages.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Partial. The Registry sentence ("governs the actors on the network and compensates Automation Nodes…") is liftable; "Upkeep" and "Automation Node" are used but not crisply defined at first use.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: No JSON-LD, missing canonical, no datePublished/dateModified (measured). Head metadata could not be captured — the CLI should pass raw `<head>` for a full read; treat this as unverified rather than certain-absent, but the JSON-LD absence is confirmed from served HTML.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: No code blocks; acceptable for a pure concept page, so no penalty beyond neutral.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Covers "how does Chainlink Automation work" and "is it reliable," but no troubleshooting, no "what is an Upkeep," no symptom-phrased entry points.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong and consistent overall; minor grammar slip: "Chainlink Automation use the same…" (should be "uses").

audit.summary: This is a short (266-word) conceptual overview of the Chainlink Automation network architecture, structured cleanly with four headings and no level skips. Its biggest strength is clarity of prose and a coherent "How it works" section that describes the OCR3 consensus flow in liftable form. Its biggest opportunity is concrete specifics: the page carries **zero numerals, zero version details, and vague quantifiers** ("significant reorgs," "some nodes") where numbers or version identifiers would carry real citation lift. The honest verdict: technically sound but thin and under-specified for generative retrieval — it explains the shape of the system without any of the quantitative or cited detail engines preferentially quote.

recommendations.title: Add concrete specifics to replace vague quantifiers
recommendations.where: "How it works" and the transaction-manager paragraph
recommendations.issue: "still perform your upkeep even if some nodes are down"; "chains with significant reorgs"
recommendations.change: State the actual fault-tolerance model (e.g. the f+1 / supermajority OCR3 threshold, node-set size) and quantify reorg depth tolerance where documented. Replace "some" and "significant" with numbers.
recommendations.why: Quantitative claims are the highest-lift GEO change; vague qualifiers are rarely quoted.

recommendations.title: Add a lead-in canonical definition
recommendations.issue: page opens with a diagram reference, not a definition.
recommendations.change: Add one liftable sentence, e.g. "Chainlink Automation is a decentralized service that uses the OCR3 protocol to reliably execute smart-contract functions (Upkeeps) when predefined conditions are met, coordinated by the onchain Automation Registry."
recommendations.why: A self-contained opening sentence is what engines lift for "what is Chainlink Automation architecture" queries.

recommendations.title: Link named technical entities to primary sources
recommendations.where: "Chainlink's OCR3 protocol," "transaction manager … used by Chainlink Data Feeds"
recommendations.change: Inline-link OCR3 to its canonical spec/docs page and the transaction manager / Data Feeds reference to their doc pages.
recommendations.why: Attributable claims raise credibility and citation rate.

recommendations.title: Add an actors summary table
recommendations.issue: no table/list; actors described only in prose.
recommendations.change: Add a 3-row table: Automation Registry / Automation Nodes / Upkeeps → role + one-line definition.
recommendations.why: Tables give engines extractable, justified units and crisp definitions.

recommendations.title: Add page metadata
recommendations.issue: no JSON-LD, no canonical, no dateModified (measured).
recommendations.change: Emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with canonical URL and a visible last-updated date.
recommendations.why: Structured metadata and freshness signals improve agent parsing and E-E-A-T — though this is lower-impact than the retrieval/specificity fixes above.

recommendations.title: Add query-phrased sub-headings
recommendations.issue: concept-titled headings ("Internal monitoring") don't match how devs ask.
recommendations.change: Consider "How does Chainlink Automation stay reliable during gas spikes and reorgs?" as an H2/H3.
recommendations.why: Question-phrased headings win retrieval that concept titles lose.

antiPatterns: Vague quantifiers: "some nodes are down," "significant reorgs" — replace with figures.
Marketing-adjacent phrasing: "industry leading reliability," "hyper-reliable" — unsupported by numbers; either quantify or trim.
Placeholder image references ("(Image: Image)") carry no alt text or caption — add descriptive captions that restate the architecture in liftable text.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced at page top — good site-level signal.
Site-level JSON-LD and canonical-URL emission should be verified against raw `<head>` (not captured here); confirm across the docs template rather than per-page.
Supported-network counts and cost figures live on linked pages — consider surfacing a headline number here to reduce the retrieval hop.
